title: Admin - Filter Admins by Role - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - Filter Admins by Role feature on the Y4J platform. This feature provides a role filter dropdown (All Roles, Super Admin, Limited-Access Admin) that dynamically updates the admin list, highlights the selected filter, and works in combination with search. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility, visual requirements, and dynamic content updates.

testCases.title: Role filter dropdown has an accessible label
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin and navigated to the Internal Administrators page with role filter
steps: Navigate to the role filter dropdown
Inspect the dropdown using a screen reader
Verify the dropdown has a programmatically associated label (via <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby)
Verify the label clearly describes the purpose (e.g., 'Filter by role')
expectedResults: Dropdown has an accessible name (e.g., 'Filter by role')
Screen reader announces the dropdown name, role ('combobox' or 'listbox'), and current value
Label is programmatically associated with the dropdown element
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users understand the purpose of the role filter

testCases.title: Role filter dropdown is operable via keyboard
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin page with role filter is loaded
steps: Press Tab to navigate to the role filter dropdown
Press Enter or Space to open the dropdown
Use Arrow Down to navigate to 'Super Admin' option
Use Arrow Up to navigate to 'All Roles' option
Press Enter to select the focused option
Press Escape to close the dropdown without selecting
expectedResults: Dropdown is reachable via Tab key
Enter/Space opens the dropdown options list
Arrow keys navigate between options (All Roles, Super Admin, Limited-Access Admin)
Enter selects the currently focused option
Escape closes the dropdown without changing selection
No mouse interaction is required
testCases.postconditions: Role filter is fully operable via keyboard

testCases.title: Role filter dropdown has visible focus indicator
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin page is loaded
steps: Tab to the role filter dropdown
Observe the focus indicator on the dropdown trigger
Open the dropdown and observe focus indicator on individual options
Navigate between options using arrow keys and observe focus movement
expectedResults: Dropdown trigger shows a clearly visible focus indicator when focused
Focus indicator has at least 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent colors
Individual options show focus/highlight indicator when navigated via keyboard
Focus indicator is not solely a color change
testCases.postconditions: Focus state is clearly visible on dropdown and its options

testCases.title: Dropdown options announce role and state to screen readers
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role filter dropdown is open
steps: Open the role filter dropdown using keyboard
Navigate to each option using arrow keys
Listen to screen reader announcements for each option
Select an option and verify the selected state is announced
Re-open the dropdown and verify the currently selected option is indicated
expectedResults: Each option is announced with its text (e.g., 'All Roles', 'Super Admin', 'Limited-Access Admin')
Options have role='option' or equivalent
Currently selected option is announced as 'selected' or 'checked'
aria-selected='true' or equivalent marks the active filter
Screen reader announces position in list (e.g., '1 of 3')
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users can identify all options and the current selection

testCases.title: Selected filter highlight does not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, a role filter is selected (e.g., 'Super Admin')
steps: Select a role filter option
Observe how the selected filter is visually highlighted
View the page in grayscale mode
Verify the selected state is still distinguishable without color
expectedResults: Selected filter uses more than just color to indicate selection (e.g., bold text, border, checkmark icon, background pattern)
In grayscale mode, selected filter is still distinguishable from unselected options
Selected state is also communicated programmatically (aria-selected, aria-current)
testCases.postconditions: Selected filter state is perceivable regardless of color vision

testCases.title: Selected filter highlight has sufficient contrast
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, a role filter is selected
steps: Select a role filter option
Use a contrast checker to measure the selected option text against its background
Measure the contrast of the highlight/border against adjacent colors
Check contrast of unselected option text as well
expectedResults: Selected option text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background
Highlight indicator (border, background) has at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors
Unselected option text also meets 4.5:1 contrast minimum
testCases.postconditions: All filter states are readable for users with low vision

testCases.title: Filtered results are announced to screen readers via aria-live
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Enable screen reader
Select 'Super Admin' from the role filter dropdown
Listen for screen reader announcement of filtered results
Select 'Limited-Access Admin' from the role filter
Listen for updated announcement
Select 'All Roles' to restore full list
Listen for restoration announcement
expectedResults: Screen reader announces the number of results after filtering (e.g., '2 Super Admin administrators found')
Announcement uses aria-live='polite' so it doesn't interrupt the user
Updated count is announced when filter changes
Restoring 'All Roles' announces the full count
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users are informed of filter result changes

testCases.title: No admins in selected role shows accessible empty state
testCases.componentElement: Empty state message for filtered results
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, a role with no assigned admins exists
steps: Select a role filter that has no administrators assigned
Verify an empty state message is displayed
Verify screen reader announces the empty state
Check that the message uses role='status' or aria-live region
expectedResults: Empty state message is visually displayed (e.g., 'No administrators found for this role')
Screen reader announces the empty state without requiring focus change
Message is within an aria-live='polite' region or has role='status'
Message text has sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum)
testCases.postconditions: All users are informed when no admins match the selected role

testCases.title: Filter selection does not cause unexpected context change
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role filter dropdown is available
steps: Focus on the role filter dropdown
Select a different role option
Verify focus remains on or near the dropdown after selection
Verify no unexpected page navigation or modal opens
Verify the admin list updates in place without full page reload
expectedResults: Focus remains on the dropdown or moves predictably after selection
No unexpected navigation occurs
No new window or modal opens unexpectedly
Admin list updates dynamically in place
User maintains their context on the page
testCases.postconditions: Filter selection updates content without disorienting the user

testCases.title: Filter and search combination maintains accessibility
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, both search and role filter are available
steps: Type a search query in the search input
Then select a role filter from the dropdown
Verify the combined results are announced to screen reader
Change the role filter while search is active
Verify updated combined results are announced
Clear the search while filter is active
Verify results update correctly
expectedResults: Combined filter+search results count is announced via aria-live
Changing filter while search is active updates results and announces new count
Clearing search while filter is active shows all admins for that role
No accessibility errors occur when combining filter and search
Focus is not unexpectedly moved during combined operations
testCases.postconditions: Filter and search work together accessibly

testCases.title: Switching filter while search is applied does not trap keyboard
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search has text entered, filter is available
steps: Type a search query in the search input
Tab to the role filter dropdown
Open the dropdown and select a different role
Tab away from the dropdown to the next element
Shift+Tab back to the dropdown
Verify focus moves freely between search and filter
expectedResults: Focus moves freely between search input and filter dropdown
No keyboard trap occurs when switching between filter and search
Tab and Shift+Tab work correctly in all states
Dropdown can be opened and closed without trapping focus
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard users can freely navigate between filter and search

testCases.title: Tab order is logical between search and filter components
testCases.componentElement: Search input and role filter tab sequence
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, page with search and filter is loaded
steps: Start at the top of the page
Tab through interactive elements
Document the order: navigation → search → filter → admin list items
Verify the order follows visual layout (left-to-right, top-to-bottom)
expectedResults: Tab order follows logical visual sequence
Search input and filter dropdown are in a predictable order
No unexpected focus jumps between search and filter
After filter, focus moves to the admin list or next logical element
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard navigation follows a predictable, logical order

testCases.title: Dropdown expanded/collapsed state is communicated
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role filter dropdown is available
steps: Focus on the role filter dropdown (closed state)
Verify screen reader announces 'collapsed' or 'closed' state
Open the dropdown
Verify screen reader announces 'expanded' or 'open' state
Close the dropdown with Escape
Verify screen reader announces return to 'collapsed' state
expectedResults: aria-expanded='false' is set when dropdown is closed
aria-expanded='true' is set when dropdown is open
Screen reader announces the expanded/collapsed state change
State transitions are immediate and accurate
testCases.postconditions: Dropdown open/close state is always communicated to assistive technology

testCases.title: Role filter is functional at 200% browser zoom
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin page is loaded
steps: Set browser zoom to 200%
Verify the role filter dropdown is fully visible
Open the dropdown and verify all options are visible without horizontal scrolling
Select an option and verify the list updates correctly
Verify the selected highlight is visible at 200%
expectedResults: Dropdown trigger is fully visible at 200% zoom
Dropdown options list does not overflow or get clipped
All option text is readable without horizontal scrolling
Selection and highlighting work correctly at 200%
No content overlap occurs
testCases.postconditions: Role filter is fully functional at 200% zoom

testCases.title: Role filter reflows correctly at 320px viewport width
testCases.componentElement: Role filter layout at narrow viewport
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin page is loaded
steps: Resize browser viewport to 320px width
Verify the role filter dropdown is accessible without horizontal scrolling
Open the dropdown and verify options are fully visible
Verify filter works correctly at narrow width
expectedResults: Role filter adapts to narrow viewport
No horizontal scrollbar is required to access the filter
Dropdown options are fully readable
Filter functionality is preserved at narrow width
testCases.postconditions: Role filter works on narrow viewports/mobile

testCases.title: Filtered admin list maintains proper semantic structure
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role filter has been applied showing subset of admins
steps: Select 'Super Admin' from the role filter
Inspect the filtered admin list structure
Verify the list still uses semantic markup (ul/ol or role='list')
Verify hidden/filtered items are removed from the DOM or have aria-hidden='true'
Navigate the filtered list with screen reader
expectedResults: Filtered list maintains semantic list structure
Screen reader announces correct item count for filtered results
Hidden admin cards are not announced by screen reader
List structure is valid (no empty list if items exist)
testCases.postconditions: Filtered list is semantically correct for assistive technologies

testCases.title: Role filter reset on page refresh maintains accessibility
testCases.componentElement: Role filter state after page refresh
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, a role filter is currently selected
steps: Select a specific role filter (e.g., 'Limited-Access Admin')
Refresh the page (F5 or Ctrl+R)
Verify the filter resets to 'All Roles'
Verify the dropdown shows 'All Roles' as selected
Verify screen reader announces the default state correctly
expectedResults: After refresh, filter resets to 'All Roles' (default)
Dropdown visually shows 'All Roles' as selected
Screen reader announces 'All Roles' as the current value
Full admin list is displayed
No stale filter state confuses assistive technology users
testCases.postconditions: Filter state is predictable after page refresh

testCases.title: Role filter dropdown touch target meets minimum size
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, page is viewed on touch device or responsive view
steps: Measure the clickable/tappable area of the role filter dropdown trigger
Measure the clickable area of each dropdown option when open
Verify adequate spacing between options
expectedResults: Dropdown trigger has at least 44x44 CSS pixels touch target
Each dropdown option has at least 44x44 CSS pixels touch target
Adequate spacing exists between options to prevent accidental selection
testCases.postconditions: Filter is usable for users with motor impairments on touch devices

testCases.title: Role filter dropdown options text has sufficient contrast
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role filter dropdown is open
steps: Open the role filter dropdown
Use a contrast checker to measure text contrast of each option against its background
Check contrast of the hover/focus state for options
Check contrast of disabled options (if any)
expectedResults: All option text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against background
Hover/focus state text maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast
Option text is readable for users with low vision
testCases.postconditions: All dropdown option text is readable

testCases.title: Filter component is within appropriate landmark region
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin page is loaded
steps: Use screen reader landmark navigation
Verify the role filter is within the main content landmark
Verify the filter is logically grouped with the admin list it controls
Check if filter has a group label (e.g., within a fieldset or role='group')
expectedResults: Role filter is within the main landmark region
Filter is logically associated with the content it controls
If grouped with other filters, the group has an accessible label
Screen reader users can locate the filter via landmark navigation
testCases.postconditions: Filter is discoverable and contextually placed for assistive technology users
